title: Al-Based Fake Identity & Document Screening System
department: Sashastra Seema Bal (SSB), Police II Division
description:
• Background Common challenges faced at border checkpoints:
• Fake passports and visas
• Altered photographs
• Modified dates of birth
• Tampered visa stamps
• Identity impersonation
• Multiple identities used by the same person Expired or blacklisted travel documents
• High passenger volume causing delays Current verification methods rely heavily on human inspection and basic database lookups.
• Detailed Description Border checkpoints process thousands of identity documents every day,including passports, visas, national identity cards, permits, and travel authorizations. Manual verification is time-consuming, prone to human error, and often unable to detect sophisticated forgeries, tampering, or identity fraud.Develop an Al-powered document screening platform that automatically analyzes identity and travel documents, detects signs of tampering or forgery, validates information against rules and databases,and generates a risk score to assist border security personnel in making faster and more accurate decisions.
• Expected Solution
• Module 1: OCR Extraction
• Module 2: Document Validation
• Module 3: Tampering Detection
• Module 4: Face Detection Module 1: OCR Extraction Objective: Automatically extract all relevant information from identity documents.
Inputs:
• Passport image
• Visa image
• National ID image
• Driving license
• Permit documents Extracted Fields:
Passport
• Name
• Passport Number
• Nationality
• Date of birth
• Date of expiry
• Gender Visa
• Visa Number
• Visa Type
• Entry Validation
• Stay Duration Module 2: Document Validation Objective: Verify whether the extracted information follows official document standards.
Module 3: Tampering Detection (Core AI Innovation)
Objective: Detect digitally or physically altered documents.
Use Cases:
• Photo Replacement
• Text Manipulation
• Stamp Forgery Detection
• Image Metadata Analysis Module 4: Face Verification Objective: Ensure document owner matches the presented individual.
• Expected Impact
• Reduce document verification time from several minutes to a few seconds.
• Improve detection of forged and tampered documents.
• Standardize screening decisions across checkpoints.
• Enable data-driven risk assessment instead of purely manual inspection.
• Create a digital trail for investigations and intelligence analysis.
Possible Project Name Al-Based Fake Identity & Document Screening System.
summary: Innovation (3/5): draws on ai applied to a miscellaneous problem, placing it in the moderate band. Feasibility (3/5): as a software build with moderate integration complexity, a full build is tight for 36 hours and will need scope-cutting. Impact (3/5): addresses a more targeted user group within Miscellaneous. Tech Depth (2/5): centers on moderate engineering scope. Sustainability (3/5): will need a maintenance/upkeep plan post-hackathon. Scalability (2/5): currently scoped narrowly and would need rework to scale. Total 16/30 -> Yellow verdict.

detail.title: AI-Based Fake Identity & Document Screening System

overview.in_plain_terms: Build a tool that scans a passport or visa photo, pulls out all the text automatically, checks it against official formats, looks for signs of digital or physical tampering, and confirms the photo actually matches the person holding it, giving a border officer a risk score in seconds instead of minutes of manual checking.
overview.why_it_matters: Border checkpoints process thousands of documents a day under time pressure, and manual inspection simply can't catch sophisticated forgeries reliably. A fast, consistent automated screening layer both speeds up legitimate travelers and catches fraud human reviewers would likely miss.
pain_points: Manual verification of passports, visas, and IDs is slow and inconsistent, and doesn't scale well against high passenger volume.
Sophisticated forgeries (photo replacement, text manipulation, stamp forgery) can be very hard for a human eye to catch under time pressure.

A useful screening tool needs to combine several distinct checks, OCR extraction, format validation, tampering detection, and face matching, into one coherent risk score, not four disconnected outputs.
overview.background: Border checkpoints process thousands of identity documents daily. Manual verification is time-consuming, prone to human error, and often unable to detect sophisticated forgeries, tampering, or identity fraud. An AI-powered document screening platform is needed that automatically analyzes identity and travel documents, detects tampering, validates against rules and databases, and generates a risk score for border security personnel.
overview.whats_being_asked: A four-module AI document screening platform: OCR Extraction (pulling structured fields from passports, visas, IDs, licenses, permits), Document Validation (checking extracted data against official standards), Tampering Detection (the core AI innovation: detecting photo replacement, text manipulation, stamp forgery, metadata anomalies), and Face Verification (matching the document photo to the presented individual), producing a consolidated risk score.
expected_solution: Module 1 - OCR Extraction: automatically extract structured fields (name, document number, nationality, DOB, expiry, etc.) from multiple document types.
Module 2 - Document Validation: verify extracted information follows official document standards/formats.
Module 3 - Tampering Detection: detect photo replacement, text manipulation, stamp forgery, and image metadata anomalies.
Module 4 - Face Verification: confirm the document photo matches the presented individual.
A consolidated risk score assisting border personnel in faster, more accurate decisions.

analysis.innovation_scope_note: Moderate band, an accurate read, OCR and face verification are largely solved problems with strong open-source tooling, the genuinely novel piece is tampering detection, which the brief itself flags as 'core AI innovation', and that's exactly where a team's real effort should concentrate.
analysis.invention_effort_note: Low, correctly scored relative to other PS in this batch, three of the four modules (OCR, validation, face verification) can lean heavily on existing open-source tools, leaving tampering detection as the one module requiring genuine model-building effort.

competitive_landscape.note: Document-forgery/OCR-based screening is a recognizable hackathon theme, but the specific four-module structure with tampering detection as the explicit centerpiece gives a disciplined team a clear way to differentiate from a generic 'OCR + database lookup' pitch.

innovation.note: OCR and face verification are well-solved problems, tampering detection (photo replacement, text manipulation, stamp forgery) is the genuinely innovative core the brief itself calls out.

invention.note: Strong open-source tooling exists for three of the four modules, real invention effort concentrates specifically on the tampering-detection module.

technical_feasibility.note: A working OCR + validation + basic tampering-detection + face-verification pipeline is realistic in 36 hours given the availability of open-source OCR and face-verification libraries.

impact_and_benefits.note: Directly benefits border security personnel and processing speed, a real but specialized user base rather than a broad citizen-facing impact.

architecture.note: Four modules chained into a single risk-scoring pipeline is a clean, well-understood architecture, the main risk is over-scoping the tampering-detection module beyond what's achievable.

overall_verdict.reasoning: A genuinely achievable pick, the OCR/validation/face-verification modules can be built fast using existing open-source tools, freeing real time to build and validate the tampering-detection module properly, since that's both the brief's stated priority and the module most likely to differentiate a submission from generic document-scanning demos.

evaluator_lens.biggest_strength: Three of the four required modules have strong, ready-to-use open-source tooling (Tesseract/EasyOCR for extraction, face_recognition/DeepFace for verification), letting the team move fast and focus real effort where it matters most.
evaluator_lens.biggest_risk: Treating all four modules as equally deep technical challenges risks spreading effort too thin, tampering detection needs disproportionate attention since it's both the hardest and the most judge-visible differentiator.
evaluator_lens.validate_before_commit: Confirm hour 0: source or create a small set of test documents including some with deliberate, visible tampering (photo swap, altered text) so you have something concrete to validate your Module 3 detection against, this is your most important test asset.

idea_0_4: Source or create test documents: sample passport/visa/ID images, plus a deliberately tampered set (photo-swapped, text-altered) for validating detection, this is your critical test asset, start immediately.
Pick your OCR and face-verification libraries (EasyOCR/Tesseract, DeepFace/face_recognition) and confirm they run correctly on your test documents before building further.
Assign owners: one on OCR+validation (Modules 1-2), one on tampering detection (Module 3, the priority module), one on face verification + risk-score aggregation (Module 4 + integration).
prototype_4_22: Build OCR extraction and field-format validation against your test document set, get this working reliably first since it's the fastest win.

Invest the majority of remaining time on tampering detection: start with image forensics techniques (error-level analysis for digital manipulation, font/spacing consistency checks for text tampering) rather than trying to train a deep model from scratch.
Build basic face verification comparing the document photo against a live/uploaded selfie.
integration_22_30: Wire all four modules into a single pipeline producing a consolidated, weighted risk score.
Test the full pipeline against your genuine and deliberately-tampered document sets, validate that tampered documents actually score meaningfully higher risk.
Build a clean officer-facing UI showing the risk score with the specific flagged concerns (which module triggered, and why).
polish_30_36: Rehearse a live demo scanning both a clean and a deliberately tampered document, showing the risk score difference clearly.
Be ready to explain your tampering-detection approach technically, this is what judges will probe hardest given the brief's framing.
Prepare an honest note on false-positive/negative risk and how a real deployment would combine this with, not replace, human judgment.
build_plan.how_to_stand_out: Bring a genuinely tampered test document to the live demo (photo swapped, text edited) and scan both it and a clean document side by side, showing the risk score difference in real time. That live, comparative proof is far more convincing than showing tampering-detection logic on a slide.

strengths: Strong open-source tooling for 3 of 4 modules means fast, reliable progress and time freed for the harder tampering-detection work.
The four-module structure gives a clear, demo-able story: input document, four checks, one risk score.
weaknesses: Genuine tampering detection (especially subtle digital manipulation) is a harder, more research-adjacent problem than the other three modules, risk of over-promising accuracy.
No access to real government identity databases means the 'Document Validation' module can only check format/structure, not true cross-database verification.

roles_needed: ML/CV engineer (tampering detection, the priority module)
Someone to source/create realistic test documents including tampered examples
team_fit.ideal_ratio: 1-2 ML-focused (weighted toward tampering detection) to 1 backend, don't split effort evenly across all four modules given their very different difficulty levels.
team_fit.approach: Get the easier three modules (OCR, validation, face verification) working with off-the-shelf tools in the first several hours, specifically to free up maximum remaining time for the harder tampering-detection module.

ai_buildability_split.ai_can_build_fast: OCR integration, format-validation rule-writing, and face-verification library integration can all be built quickly with AI coding assistance.
ai_buildability_split.needs_human_judgment: Deciding which forensic signals (metadata inconsistency, compression artifacts, font irregularities) are actually reliable tampering indicators, versus false-positive-prone noise, needs real testing against your own tampered test set, not assumptions.
ai_buildability_split.risk_of_leaning_on_ai_only: An AI-generated 'tampering detection' module that was never tested against an actual tampered document, and only demoed on clean documents scoring 'low risk', proves nothing, the whole point of this module is catching the tampered case, test against it explicitly.

data_resource_availability.status: Open-source OCR (Tesseract, EasyOCR) and face-verification (DeepFace, face_recognition) libraries are freely available and well-documented; real government document databases and genuine forged-document datasets are not publicly accessible for this use case.
data_resource_availability.backup_plan: If sourcing enough varied test documents is hard, create your own using stock ID-template images and basic photo editing to introduce deliberate tampering, a small, clearly-labeled synthetic test set is a legitimate and honest substitute.

judge_qna.question: How does your tampering detection actually work, technically?
judge_qna.strong_answer: We used [specific technique, e.g. error-level analysis to detect recompression artifacts from photo replacement, or font-consistency checks for text tampering], here's a side-by-side example of it flagging a document we deliberately tampered with.
judge_qna.follow_up: What's your false-positive rate against genuine, unaltered documents with natural image noise or compression?

judge_qna.question: Without access to real government ID databases, how do you validate document authenticity, not just internal format consistency?
judge_qna.strong_answer: We're upfront that our Document Validation module checks structural/format consistency, not cross-database authenticity, a real deployment would integrate with actual government verification databases, which weren't accessible for a hackathon build.
judge_qna.follow_up: What would that database integration need to look like, and what are the data-sharing/security implications?

judge_qna.question: How would this system handle a country's document format it wasn't trained on?
judge_qna.strong_answer: Our OCR and validation modules are built to be format-configurable, adding a new document template means adding its field layout, not retraining the core system, though tampering detection would need format-specific tuning for best accuracy.
judge_qna.follow_up: What's the actual process and time cost to onboard a new document type in your architecture?
